summary: Implemented bundled Surfaces A-E of the HATP Trust-Enrollment Implementation Capability: Fido2HardwareProvider.enroll_credential() (Surface A, deterministic tests via monkeypatched CtapHidDevice/Ctap2, no real hardware); hatp_hardware_credential_admin.py, the HHCE-001 writer with its own .hardware-credential-transition.lock (Surface B); hatp_principal_signer_admin.py, the HPSE-001 writer whose enroll_signer holds the hardware-credential lock (outer) and .deployment-binding-transition.lock (inner) continuously across its entire check-to-write critical section, structurally closing HPSE-REQ-056's cross-registry precondition (Surface C, HHCE-REQ-037 -- verified both by source-order assertion and by fcntl.flock instrumentation proving a strict nested acquire/acquire/release/release sequence, plus a 6-thread concurrency test converging on exactly one ENROLLED outcome); PrincipalRecord.revoked_at schema widening (Surface D); DeploymentBinding producer cross-validation against the Principal/Signer/hardware-credential registries and HBDC-001's closed authority_scope vocabulary, with AuthorityEvidence.provider_profile removed and derived instead (Surface E, HPSE-REQ-048). HHCE-001 repaired in place to v1.1 (HHCE-REQ-002 corrected: public_key is CBOR-encoded COSE_Key bytes, not DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo -- closes NBF-149O.20L.7O.2E.1-1). 46 new focused/adversarial tests (tests/test_hatp_trust_enrollment_capability.py) plus a rewritten tests/test_hatp_deployment_binding_admin.py (54 tests) all pass. Affected-regression sweeps (-k hatp and full -m fast_green -n auto), each diffed against an isolated git-worktree phase-entry baseline, show only the expected HMIC-bound-file byte-identity/no-production-source-modified test family as net-new failures, plus two independently-reproduced pre-existing-on-baseline failures and one confirmed -n auto-only flake; every net-new failure was individually inspected, not merely asserted. Genuine regressions found during this phase were fixed in production code/tests, not left as unexplained.

validation_results.name: surface_a_fido2_enroll_credential_deterministic
validation_results.result: Fido2HardwareProvider.enroll_credential() implemented via real CTAP2 makeCredential ceremony; deterministic tests via monkeypatched CtapHidDevice/Ctap2 (no real hardware); no-device, cancelled, device-error, and no-credential-data paths all tested; credential_identity() deliberately left unchanged (distinct discovery-vs-enrollment operation).

validation_results.name: surface_b_hhce_writer_idempotent_conflict_revocation_lock
validation_results.result: register_credential/revoke_credential/preview pair implemented; idempotency, conflict-on-differing-fields, revoked-never-reactivates, monotonic idempotent revocation, .hardware-credential-transition.lock (0o600, fcntl.flock), symlink rejection, and read-back verification all directly tested.

validation_results.name: surface_c_continuous_two_lock_critical_section
validation_results.result: enroll_signer's hardware-credential lock (outer) / .deployment-binding-transition.lock (inner) nesting verified structurally (source-order assertion) and at runtime (fcntl.flock instrumentation proving a strict acquire/acquire/release/release sequence for one call, distinguishable from a release/reacquire violation pattern); 6-thread concurrent enrollment test converges on exactly one ENROLLED outcome.

validation_results.name: cross_registry_invariant_hpse_req_056
validation_results.result: enroll_signer re-checks the hardware-credential precondition immediately before and after the write, under the continuously-held lock pair; enrollment without a registered credential fails closed (HardwareCredentialNotRegisteredError) and leaves no SignerRecord.

validation_results.name: surface_d_principal_revoked_at_schema
validation_results.result: PrincipalRecord widened with revoked_at; backward-compatible for active records without the key; correctly rejects revoked-without-revoked_at and active-with-revoked_at as malformed.

validation_results.name: surface_e_deployment_binding_cross_validation
